_documentation: This file centralizes every heuristic weight and assumption the optimizer uses. Nothing here is a verified game formula — all of it is an explicit, editable design choice (HEURISTIC / ASSUMPTION tier from OPTIMIZER_MODEL.md), kept in one place instead of scattered as magic numbers across the codebase. Edit these numbers to retune recommendations; no code changes required.

pictoStatReferenceScale._documentation: Divisors used to bring Health/Defense/Critical Rate/Speed onto a comparable scale before applying strategy weights. Without this, Health (which is stored in the hundreds/thousands) would always dominate scoring over Critical Rate/Speed (stored in the tens) regardless of strategy profile, purely because of unit magnitude — not because it's actually more valuable for that strategy. These are rough, editable heuristic constants, not verified game values.

scalingGradeWeight._documentation: How strongly a weapon's S/A/B/C/D scaling grade on an attribute should influence that attribute's suggested priority. This is our own scoring convention, not an in-game number — the game does not publish a numeric value per grade letter.

attributeAllocationFloorRatio._documentation: Fraction of the point budget reserved and spread evenly across all 5 attributes before the remainder is allocated by weight, so the optimizer never suggests reducing any attribute to exactly zero. This is a heuristic guardrail we chose for build stability, not a game rule.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: No strategic tilt — equal weight on every attribute and Picto/Lumina category. Useful as a neutral baseline or when you don't know a character's role yet.

damage.label: Damage
damage.description: Favors raw offense: Might, Agility (turn speed / more actions) and Luck (crit rate), at the expense of Vitality/Defense.

defensive.label: Defensive
defensive.description: Favors survivability: Vitality and Defense, with a smaller Agility allowance for turn order, at the expense of Might/Luck.

break.label: Break
break.description: Favors attributes generally associated with filling/breaking the Break bar (frequent, high-hit-count offense) — Agility and Might, with Luck for crit-driven Break contributions. This profile is a more speculative guess than the others: Phase 1B research did not turn up a dedicated, sourced breakdown of the Break mechanic's attribute scaling, so treat its weights as a rougher starting point to hand-tune.

status_burn.label: Burn / Mark
status_burn.description: Favors Luck (crit rate, and per one source possibly status-effect chance) for Burn/Mark-oriented builds, with Support-leaning Luminas. As of Phase 2.2B, Pictos/Luminas that structurally apply Burn, apply Mark, or benefit from a Burning/Marked target get a small heuristic relevance bonus and an explained reason; other named statuses (Stun, Shell, Powerful, Regen, Slow, etc.) are intentionally not modeled by this profile.

custom.label: Custom
custom.description: Starts identical to Balanced. Edit the weights in data/optimizer_reference.json under strategyProfiles.custom to define your own strategy without touching any code.

genericWeaponScalingThresholdLevels.confidence: generic community-cited approximation, not a verified per-weapon table
genericWeaponScalingThresholdLevels._documentation: Commonly-cited levels at which weapon scaling grades and passives tend to step up, per Phase 1B research (Game8/Maxroll/KeenGamer/GamerGuides). No source gave a single authoritative per-weapon table, so this is shown to the user as an approximate, labeled reference only — never used as if it were exact for a specific weapon.

knownUnknowns: No verified formula converts a scaling grade + attribute points into an exact damage or DPS number. The optimizer must never state one.
Per-weapon exact scaling-grade transition levels (only the generic 4/10/20/33 approximation above is available).
Weapon passive effects and unlock levels are missing for almost all weapons in data/weapons.json (left as empty arrays) — not populated for v0.1.
Skill mechanical effects are flavor text only (src/assets/characters.json), not structured numeric data — skills are intentionally outside the optimizer for v0.1.

Whether unlocking a Picto as a Lumina also grants its attribute bonus table (which otherwise only applies when a Picto is equipped in one of the 3 Picto slots) is unverified. The Lumina optimizer therefore scores Luminas only by their 'type' category (Offensive/Defensive/Support) and strategy fit, never by the attribute-bonus table, to avoid conflating two mechanics that may not both apply.

Structured Picto/Lumina effect tags (data/picto_effects.json, Phase 2.2A) describe which mechanics/triggers/effects a Picto's text references — not combat strength. The Break-profile bonus below is a HEURISTIC relevance signal, not a measured damage contribution; see OPTIMIZER_MODEL.md.

breakEffectModel._documentation: Phase 2.2A: an additive HEURISTIC bonus applied ONLY when strategyProfile is 'break', using structured effect tags from data/picto_effects.json (see src/optimizer/breakEffectModel.ts) instead of relying solely on the Offensive/Defensive/Support category and generic stat weights. Every other strategy profile is unaffected — this bonus is never applied outside the Break profile. Both constants are our own scoring convention (not a verified game value), chosen to be a meaningful nudge without overriding the existing stat-based/category-based score entirely.

statusBurnEffectModel._documentation: Phase 2.2B: an additive HEURISTIC bonus applied ONLY when strategyProfile is 'status_burn' (labeled "Burn / Mark" in the UI), using structured Burn/Mark-only effect tags from data/picto_effects.json (see src/optimizer/statusBurnEffectModel.ts) instead of relying solely on the Offensive/Defensive/Support category and generic stat weights. Deliberately scoped to Burn and Mark only — a record merely mentioning the generic status_effect mechanic, or any other named status (Stun, Shell, Powerful, Regen, Slow, Defenceless, Powerless, Charm, Blight, Freeze, Inverted), earns zero bonus here (see the post-2.2A Stun correction for why). Every other strategy profile is unaffected. Item-local only — does not consider whether a producer/consumer counterpart is present elsewhere in the current build (see OPTIMIZER_MODEL.md). Both constants are our own scoring convention (not a verified game value), matching the Break bonus's magnitude for consistency.
